description: President Obama and Republican nominee Mitt Romney met in Denver for the first of three presidential debates, focused on domestic policy. Commentators across the spectrum described Romney as aggressive and well prepared and Obama as subdued. Instant polls of viewers found most thought Romney performed better.

The Washington Post published a 2005 recording in which Republican nominee Donald Trump boasted in vulgar terms about groping women. Trump issued a videotaped apology calling the remarks locker-room talk. Several Republican officeholders withdrew their endorsements and some called on him to leave the race.

measure: vote margin, poll average (ceiling; decline began earlier)
description: FBI Director James Comey told congressional leaders in a letter that the bureau had found emails that might be pertinent to its closed investigation of Hillary Clinton's private server and would review them. The letter gave no details on their content or significance. The Clinton campaign demanded that the FBI release more information.

Attorney General William Barr sent Congress a four-page summary of Special Counsel Robert Mueller's report. Barr said the investigation did not establish that the Trump campaign conspired with Russia and did not reach a conclusion on obstruction of justice, which Barr judged insufficient to charge. President Trump called it complete exoneration.

House Speaker Nancy Pelosi announced a formal impeachment inquiry into President Trump. It followed a whistleblower complaint about a July call in which Trump asked Ukraine's president to investigate Joe Biden. The White House released a memo of the call the next day.

measure: approval of Republican president (Gallup adjacent waves)
description: President Trump declared a national emergency over the spreading coronavirus, freeing up to $50 billion in federal aid. The declaration followed the WHO's pandemic designation, suspension of the NBA season and a ban on most travel from Europe. States began closing schools and limiting gatherings.

measure: approval of Republican president (Pew panel; upper bound)
description: A crowd of President Trump's supporters stormed the U.S. Capitol after a rally near the White House, forcing lawmakers to halt certification of the Electoral College results and evacuate. Five people died in connection with the events. Congress certified Joe Biden's victory early the next morning.

Taliban fighters entered Kabul and President Ashraf Ghani fled Afghanistan, as the Afghan government collapsed ahead of the U.S. withdrawal deadline. Crowds of Afghans rushed the Kabul airport trying to leave. The Pentagon sent thousands of troops to secure evacuation flights.

measure: generic ballot margin, same-pollster pairs over 2 weeks
description: The Supreme Court overturned Roe v. Wade in Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization, ending the constitutional right to abortion and returning the issue to the states. Trigger laws banning most abortions took effect in several states within hours. Protests formed outside the Court.

A Manhattan jury found former President Donald Trump guilty on all 34 felony counts of falsifying business records to conceal a hush-money payment before the 2016 election. He is the first former president convicted of a crime. Trump called the trial rigged and said he would appeal; sentencing was set for July 11.

President Biden and former President Trump met in Atlanta for the first debate of the 2024 campaign, hosted by CNN. Biden spoke hoarsely, lost his train of thought several times and gave halting answers; Trump made numerous false statements. Several Democratic commentators publicly questioned whether Biden should remain the nominee.

A gunman opened fire at a Donald Trump campaign rally in Butler, Pennsylvania, wounding Trump in the ear and killing one attendee before being shot dead by the Secret Service. Trump was photographed raising his fist as agents led him off stage. Leaders of both parties condemned the attack.

Vice President Kamala Harris and former President Donald Trump met in Philadelphia for their only presidential debate, hosted by ABC News. Harris pressed Trump on abortion, January 6 and his rallies; Trump focused on immigration and inflation and repeated a false claim about migrants eating pets. Most instant polls of viewers judged Harris the winner.

President Trump announced sweeping 'reciprocal' tariffs at a White House event he called Liberation Day: a 10% baseline tariff on nearly all imports and higher rates on dozens of countries. Stock markets fell sharply over the next two days.

measure: approval of Republican president (Gallup; low attribution)
description: The Justice Department and FBI released a memo concluding that Jeffrey Epstein kept no 'client list' and died by suicide, and said no further files would be made public. Several prominent conservative commentators and some Republican lawmakers criticized the decision. President Trump urged supporters to move on from the issue.

The federal government shut down after Congress failed to pass funding, with Democrats demanding an extension of expiring Affordable Care Act subsidies and Republicans seeking a short-term bill without it. Hundreds of thousands of federal workers were furloughed. Leaders of both parties blamed each other.

measure: approval of Republican president (0 to +4, faded)
description: U.S. forces carried out a military operation in Venezuela and captured President Nicolas Maduro, who was flown to the United States to face narcotics-trafficking charges. President Trump announced the operation from the White House. Several Democrats questioned its legal basis and the lack of congressional authorization.

measure: approval of Republican president, immediate (null rally)
description: The United States and Israel launched coordinated air strikes across Iran targeting military infrastructure and leadership. Iranian state media reported that Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei and other senior officials were killed. Iran vowed retaliation, and oil prices jumped when markets opened.

Weeks into the U.S.-Iran conflict, shipping through the Strait of Hormuz was disrupted and U.S. gasoline prices rose from about $2.98 a gallon in late February to $3.84 by March 18. Administration officials said relief at the pump was coming.
